# Results — Study 251 (Crypto-Reversal) on a real public crypto panel

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). We rebuild the QuantNest-7
paper's price-only REV factor on a free yfinance panel: each day rank tokens by their
trailing 21-day return (one-day skip), long the bottom quintile and short the top
(**reversal**), or the reverse (**momentum**). Equal-weight legs, reformed daily. Cash-free
long-short. All figures annualised on 365 days/year (crypto never closes). As-of **2026-06-15**.*

## Data stamp

| Universe | Window | tokens | LS days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|--:|--:|---|
| 20 liquid non-stablecoin tokens (yfinance) | 2019-01-01 → 2026-06-14 | 20 | 2,700 | `6ff538381541` |

Tokens: ADA, ALGO, ATOM, BCH, BNB, BTC, DASH, DOGE, EOS, ETC, ETH, LINK, LTC, NEO, TRX,
VET, XLM, XMR, XRP, ZEC (all `-USD`). This is a **survivor** universe — tokens alive and
liquid today, projected backward (LUNA, FTT and the dead 2021 alt-L1s are absent). The same
survivorship the paper concedes inflates *its* factor returns inflates ours, and it
disproportionately flatters the momentum (winner-continuation) side.

## The headline: the paper's reversal reverses

The 21-day cross-sectional long-short, gross of costs:

| Arm | Ann. return | Sharpe | Vol | MaxDD | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Reversal** (long losers, short winners) | **−61.6%** | **−0.826** | 75% | −99.9% | **−2.10** |
| **Momentum** (long winners, short losers) | **+61.6%** | **+0.826** | 75% | −95.7% | **+2.10** |
| Shuffle control (null) | +1.6% | +0.035 | 45% | −74.8% | +0.10 |

**Fama-MacBeth** (daily cross-sectional regression of return on the lagged standardized
signal, the paper's own Table-8 apparatus): average slope **+7.15 bps/day**, Newey-West
**t = +2.44**. A *positive* slope means recent **winners** earn more — i.e. a **momentum**
premium of ≈ +26%/yr, the *opposite sign* to the paper's REV factor (which it reports as a
positive reversal premium, *t* = +6.19). The shuffle control earns ~0 (*t* = +0.10),
confirming the ranking — not the leg structure — carries the (momentum) information.

> **On this public panel the QuantNest-7 headline does not replicate. The cross-section is
> priced by momentum, not reversal — the sign reverts to Liu et al. (2022), exactly the
> result the paper claimed to overturn.**

## The cross-section IS predictable — across every horizon, the wrong way for the paper

Reversal long-short, gross, by lookback (the paper's Table 11, which reported reversal
*strongest at short horizons*):

| Lookback | Ann. return | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 7 days | −84.8% | −1.293 | −3.34 |
| 14 days | −90.4% | −1.366 | −3.47 |
| 21 days* | −61.6% | −0.826 | −2.10 |
| 42 days | −66.4% | −0.905 | −2.39 |
| 63 days | −56.6% | −0.791 | −2.16 |

*Q-7 specification. Reversal loses at **every** horizon, and (mirror-imaging the paper)
momentum is *strongest at short horizons* — the precise opposite of the paper's claim.

## Even the winning side (momentum) is a mirage after costs

The book reforms every day on a 21-day signal: one-way turnover **37.8%/day** (≈138%/yr).
Momentum long-short, net of one-way transaction cost:

| One-way cost | Ann. return | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +61.6% | +0.826 | +2.10 |
| 10 bps | +47.8% | +0.641 | +1.62 |
| 30 bps | +20.2% | +0.271 | +0.68 |
| 50 bps | −7.4% | −0.100 | −0.25 |
| 100 bps | −76.5% | −1.023 | −2.55 |

The paper itself notes crypto bid-ask spreads "can exceed 1% per trade" for smaller tokens.
At **100 bps** the momentum spread is −76.5%/yr. Even at a generous 50 bps it is already
negative. The reversal arm is worse at every cost. There is no tradable cross-sectional
spread here once you pay crypto's turnover — and shorting the small-cap leg is often
infeasible to begin with.

## Sub-era stability (reversal arm, gross / net 50 bps)

| Era | Gross Sharpe | Gross *t* | Net-50bps Sharpe | Net-50bps ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 2019-2020 | −1.221 | −1.65 | −2.177 | −153.1% |
| 2021-2022 | −0.313 | −0.41 | −1.045 | −101.7% |
| 2023-2026 | −1.193 | −1.94 | −2.391 | −138.8% |

Reversal loses in every era (so momentum *wins* in every era), but the momentum side never
clears |*t*| ≥ 2 in any single era and is near-flat in the choppy 2021-2022 top — fragile
even before costs and even before survivorship is netted out.

## Synthetic controls — the engine is correct

| Synthetic tape | Reversal Sharpe (*t*) | Momentum Sharpe | Fama-MacBeth *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Planted reversal (`signal_strength=1`) | +0.956 (+2.39) | −0.956 | −2.40 |
| Null (`signal_strength=0`) | +0.316 (+0.78) | −0.316 | −0.81 |

When a reversal *is* planted, the engine recovers it (reversal arm positive and significant,
FM slope negative). On the null tape nothing significant appears. So the **negative** reversal
sign on the real tape is not an engine artefact — it is genuine cross-sectional momentum.

## A caveat that cuts toward the paper, and against tradability

Our 20-token universe is the *most liquid survivors*. Classical short-term reversal lives in
the **small, illiquid tail** — precisely the tokens free data cannot see *and* precisely the
tokens that are uninvestable (wide spreads, no borrow). So the paper's reversal may well exist
where we cannot look — but if it does, it lives exactly where the >1% spreads make it
untradable. Either way the practitioner conclusion is the same.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE (for the reversal claim).** The paper's REV factor does not replicate on
  free data: the 21-day cross-sectional spread is *momentum*, not reversal (Fama-MacBeth
  slope +7.15 bps/day, *t* = +2.44; reversal long-short *t* = −2.10). The paper's *t* = +6.19
  reversal premium flips sign back to Liu et al. (2022) momentum on a public survivor panel.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** ~38%/day one-way turnover. The only profitable side (momentum)
  is gone by ~50 bps one-way (−7.4%/yr) and −76.5%/yr at the paper's own >100 bps crypto
  spread; the short leg (small-cap winners) is often unborrowable. No tradable spread survives.
- **Reversal or momentum? — MOMENTUM.** On public, liquid, survivor data the Liu et al.
  momentum sign holds, not the paper's reversal — and even that momentum is survivorship-
  flattered and never clears the inference bar era-by-era.
